history.summary: CSV corrected: the fort is at Khimsar (also spelled Kheenvsar; the CSV spelling 'Khinvsar' is non-standard), a town ~45 km from Nagaur in Nagaur district - not Nagaur town itself. Khimsar Fort was founded in 1523 by Prince Rao Karamsiji of the Karamsot dynasty and is now a heritage hotel run by the royal family. 'Khinvsar Fort Temple' is a generic label: the fort complex holds several places of worship - a Shiv Mandir, a Krishna Mandir, and (per the IGNCA/ASI report RJ/NGR-150) an important group of Hindu and Jain god/goddess statues at the fort itself dated 8th-10th century AD, several of them defaced. The fort's royal chapel tradition and the town's Lakshminath Ji temple nearby make this a living Hindu devotional site despite the fort's hotel conversion. Note: do not confuse Khimsar Fort with the famous Nagaur Fort (Ahhichatragarh) in Nagaur town. No verifiable photograph of a specific 'fort temple' could be found, so media is intentionally empty.
